title: Step 36: Alternating-rod Weyl regularity analysis
scope: Structural question for collapsed P4+ route

S2xS2_rectangle.smooth_metric: Round product S²(1)×S²(1), which IS Einstein

k2_hexagon.note: For k≥2, the Delzant polygon has 2+2k edges. NOT all edges need have the alternating (1,0)/(0,1) pattern; the standard Delzant realization uses more general primitive vectors. But the diagonal model studied in Steps 12-25 imposes the alternating pattern.

distinction_from_Israel_Khan.Israel_Khan: In the Israel-Khan problem, all rods collapse the SAME S¹. Adjacent bolts are both S² fixed sets of the SAME U(1). Between them, the axis has a conical singularity (strut).
distinction_from_Israel_Khan.alternating_toric: In the alternating toric model, adjacent rods collapse DIFFERENT S¹ factors. Between them (at the NUT/corner), BOTH circles degenerate to give a fixed point. There is NO axis segment between bolts where one circle is regular; instead, the transition goes through a NUT (codimension-4 point).
distinction_from_Israel_Khan.critical_consequence: A NUT is a POINT, not a codimension-2 surface. It does NOT have a cone angle. The Israel-Khan strut (codimension-2 conical deficit) is not the same object as a NUT (codimension-4 fixed point). The edge-cone defect term (1-β)χ(Σ) applies to codimension-2 singularities Σ, not to isolated points. For a NUT, the relevant singularity is an orbifold point, which contributes to χ through the orbifold Euler characteristic, not through an edge-cone term.

strut_free_examples.multi_Taub_NUT: The Gibbons-Hawking multi-center gravitational instantons are smooth, Ricci-flat, self-dual (W⁻=0), ALF/ALE metrics with multiple NUT centers. These have NO struts. They are toric and have alternating rod labels. Example: multi-Eguchi-Hanson on resolved ALE spaces.
strut_free_examples.Euclidean_Schwarzschild: A single Euclidean Schwarzschild has one smooth bolt and one asymptotic end. It is NOT self-dual and has both W⁺ and W⁻ nonzero. It is a single-rod solution with no strut.
strut_free_examples.two_Schwarzschild_on_same_axis: Two Euclidean Schwarzschild solutions on the same axis (same circle collapsing) REQUIRE an Israel-Khan strut between them. This is the standard same-label obstruction.
strut_free_examples.alternating_rods_key_question: For an alternating-label periodic array, the NUTs between rods are codimension-4 points, not codimension-2 struts. The regularity condition at each NUT is that both fiber functions vanish at the correct rate. Whether this can be satisfied globally in a periodic Ricci-flat solution is the key open question.

strut_vs_nut_reframing.for_alternating_labels: In the alternating-label toric model, the potential singularities are NUTs (codimension-4 fixed points), NOT struts (codimension-2 edge-cone). The Atiyah-LeBrun edge-cone formulas do NOT apply to NUT singularities. NUT singularities are orbifold-type points that enter the Gauss-Bonnet through the orbifold Euler characteristic correction, not through (1-β)χ(Σ) terms.
strut_vs_nut_reframing.consequence_for_energy_budget: The strut smoothing energy estimate ∫|Rm|² ~ (1-β)²|Σ|/ε² applies to codimension-2 deficits. A NUT is a POINT singularity with curvature concentrated in a ball of radius ε, giving ∫|Rm|² ~ 1/ε⁴ × ε⁴ = O(1) in 4D. So NUT smoothing costs O(1), not O(√A).
strut_vs_nut_reframing.revised_dichotomy: If the collapsed α-family has ALTERNATING labels (which it does for the diagonal toric model on #_k(S²×S²)), then the singularities are NUTs, not struts. The energy budget is: χ bolts × 8π² + χ nuts × O(1) ≤ 8π²χ. This is satisfied if the O(1) NUT energy is small enough. The OBSTRUCTION from divergent strut smoothing does NOT apply in this case.
strut_vs_nut_reframing.warning: This analysis assumes the alternating-label model. If some other collapse mode produces same-label adjacent rods (through a topology change or non-toric collapse), the strut analysis would apply. Also, the NUT smoothing O(1) estimate is crude and should be checked.

what_this_changes.collapsed_front_status: The collapsed α-family adversary is NOT killed by the strut energy argument because it has alternating labels and NUT (not strut) singularities. The honest status is: the formal toric family with alternating labels and growing edge curvature A satisfies ALL checked local, integral, and CGB conditions. No global smooth metric has been constructed, but no topology-uniform energy obstruction has been found either.
what_would_kill_it: A global Ricci-flat periodic solution with alternating labels → BREAK (requires separate Einstein nonexistence)
A topological obstruction from NUT-type orbifold constraints
A higher-order PDE obstruction in the nonlinear filling of the formal model
A new integral identity that constrains NUT curvature more tightly
what_this_changes.what_would_be_BREAK: A smooth collapsing family on #_k(S²×S²) with Ric→g is a BREAK for the positive collapsed branch only if #_k(S²×S²) admits no Einstein metric of any sign. No such nonexistence result is known.
